verdicts.reason: The spec point is correct: ES Math.sin is 'implementation-approximated' (verified), arithmetic and sqrt are exact. But (a) no cross-engine run was done; the experiment used V8 only and shows sensitivity to perturbation/order, not engine disagreement; (b) the proposal claim C-089 itself offers 'or a server is authoritative', so the hazard only applies to lockstep designs; (c) the 6e4x amplification is one 3-source velocity-Verlet scenario, dt=0.001, single run, and does not generalise to other setups. Settles it: run the same script on SpiderMonkey/JSC, or just use a server-authoritative design.
verdicts.supported_claim: ECMAScript does not guarantee bit-identical Math.sin/cos across engines, so a lockstep client-side n-body sim using them cannot be assumed to agree; in one V8 scenario a 1e-12 perturbation grew to 5.9e-8 over 1e5 steps. Cross-browser divergence itself is unmeasured; server-authoritative state avoids it.
checked: Fetched tc39.es/ecma262: Math.sin 'implementation-approximated Number value' verified.
Did not re-run nbody.js (not needed to test the spec claim); noted it ran on V8/node only.

verdicts.reason: 'Mismatch' is not shown: the restricted three-body setup the proposal likely means (analytic-orbit primaries, massless ship stepped numerically) is exactly the arXiv model quoted and the finding's own note says so. What stands is that the brief/proposal omits body count, dt and accuracy budget (C-194), and that the ship is stepped, not closed-form. Yoshida quotes support symplectic energy behaviour only for fixed step. Experiment is one scenario on one engine.
verdicts.supported_claim: Kepler gives closed-form state only for two-body orbits; a massless ship in a restricted n-body field must be numerically stepped, with error accumulating; body count, dt and error budget are unspecified. No proof that the two models conflict in the proposal.
checked: Did not re-fetch arXiv/Yoshida (quotes plausible and unchallenged; domain knowledge consistent).
Experiment not re-run.

verdicts.reason: Float addition non-associativity is true but JS fixes evaluation order, so every client running the same code sums identically. Divergence needs different code paths (server vs client rewrite, iteration over unordered collections). Measured effect is one V8 scenario (3 sources, 1e5 steps, 9.65e-10). The finding duplicates F-036 with a weaker cause.
verdicts.supported_claim: Reordering three gravity terms changed ship position by ~1e-9 after 1e5 steps in one V8 run; matters only if different clients/server sum in different orders, avoided by a fixed body-index order in shared code.
checked: Fetched tc39.es: Number type is IEEE binary64 (consistent with finding); did not re-run script.
